data_quality_warnings: NANO-CAP: market capitalisation is approximately NZ$11.4m (66,377,342 shares at NZ$0.172), far below any conventional small-cap threshold. Valuation precision at this scale should not be over-interpreted.
NEGATIVE SHAREHOLDERS' EQUITY: NZ$(1.897)m at FY2026 (NZ$(2.891)m FY2025). No P/B or book-value-based valuation method is usable; WACC carries a +2.0pp negative-equity/going-concern premium.

FY2026 reported revenue growth of +84-87% is a CONSOLIDATION/MIX effect (company-managed Dairygold/Tesco Ireland stores now book full store sales as revenue vs royalty-only for franchised stores), NOT organic growth. Reported-revenue CAGR is NOT used as the DCF growth driver -- system-wide store sales / franchise-ex-Dairygold growth (~22-23%, decelerating) is used instead. See historical_growth.notes.

OPERATING CASH FLOW DATA-QUALITY ISSUE: CCC.NZ_Metrics.csv OperatingCashFlow/FreeCashFlow values for FY2025 (0.422/0.056) and FY2026 (0.496/-0.247) do NOT match the primary Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows in the filings (FY2025 OCF = -$0.274m; FY2026 OCF = $5.122m, of which $4.147m is a one-off reclassification of 'principal elements of lease receipts' into operating activities that was previously presented in investing activities -- see valuation_philosophy). This DCF is built from the primary financial statements directly, NOT from the CSV's OCF/FCF columns, and the CSV should be corrected in a future data-pipeline pass.

MARGIN COLLAPSE FROM MIX SHIFT: gross margin fell from 94.2% (FY2025) to 86.8% (FY2026) and net margin from 12.1% to 3.2% as low-margin company-managed store revenue displaces high-margin franchise royalty revenue in the mix. Forward EBITDA margins are modelled as compressing near-term before recovering modestly as the franchise (asset-light, royalty) network reasserts scale via the 300-store FY2034 target.

Reported FCF has been negative or near breakeven in 4 of the last 5 fiscal years on a basis consistent with the primary cash flow statements; there is essentially no positive free cash flow history to extrapolate. The valuation is built on a component EBITDA-to-FCF bridge (Step 1c), not on extrapolating a reported FCF trend.

inputs.net_debt_basis: bank debt (NZ$2.860m) less cash (NZ$1.123m) only. IFRS16 lease liabilities (NZ$27.686m) are excluded from net debt because they are offset almost 1:1 by matching lease receivables (NZ$25.148m) from subleasing to franchisees -- CCC is a pass-through intermediate lessee/lessor, not a net lease-indebted operator. The NZ$2.538m net lease exposure is disclosed as a memo item and its ANNUAL cash cost (principal + interest, net of what CCC receives back from franchisee subleases) is charged as a recurring operating cash outflow inside the owner-FCF build instead (see projections.base.lease_net_cash).
inputs.reported_fcf_fy2026_note: As shown in CCC.NZ_Metrics.csv (OCF 0.496 - CapEx 0.743). This OCF figure does not reconcile to the primary FY2026 Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows (OCF $5.122m, of which $4.147m is a reclassified lease-receipt inflow not present in the FY2025 comparative presentation). See data_quality_warnings.
inputs.underlying_fcf_basis: FY2026 OCF ($5.122m as filed) less the $4.147m 'principal elements of lease receipts' that FY2026 alone reclassified into operating activities (FY2022-25 all presented this line in investing activities), less CapEx ($0.743m). This produces a comparable, non-inflated FY2026 FCF of $0.232m used as an independent cross-check of the component-built owner FCF.
inputs.last_fcf_note: The DCF's Year-1 owner FCF (NZ$0.538m) is built bottom-up from EBITDA (Step 1c component build: normalised-ish EBITDA margin 11.5% x Y1 revenue) less D&A, net lease cash cost, bank interest, cash tax (0%), CapEx, plus working capital -- NOT a single historical FCF figure grown at a flat rate. See projections.base for the full year-by-year bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: Confirmed NIL: CCC.NZ_Metrics.csv StockBasedComp = 0 in all recent years (FY2022-2026); no share-based payment expense line found in the FY2026 annual report P&L or notes.
inputs.interest_income_treatment: NOT stripped as excess-cash interest. This is IFRS16 finance-lease sublease interest income (CCC subleases premises to franchisees; interest income on the lease receivable is the economic mirror of interest expense on the matching lease liability). Confirmed by the financial-parser: kpis.InterestIncome = sublease income, not investment income on a cash pile (cash is only NZ$1.123m, immaterial). Both the interest income (P&L) and interest expense on leases (finance cost) are handled together via the 'net lease cash cost' and 'net lease interest' components inside the owner-FCF build, not stripped as if this were excess cash.
inputs.dilution_note: FY2026 saw 1,680,672 new ordinary shares issued (2.5% of year-end count) for NZ$123k proceeds -- small, continuous equity issuance, consistent with the FY2022-2026 share count CAGR (53.06m to 66.38m, ~5.8%/yr, 1-for-15 consolidation-adjusted). No buybacks in the disclosed history (ShareRepurchases = 0 all years). Modelled at 3.5%/yr base (moderating slightly from the historical 5.8%/yr as the company nears sustained profitability), 2.5%/yr bull (self-funding), 5.0%/yr bear (continued cash-strapped dilution).
inputs.horizon_rationale: 10-year horizon used because the base-case owner-FCF margin is still maturing through Year 7 (peak ~7.3%) before flattening; a 5-year horizon would capitalise an immature, still-compressed margin. See projections.base.owner_fcf_margin.

valuation_philosophy: Cooks Coffee Company cannot be valued with a conventional Gordon-growth FCF DCF anchored on trailing reported FCF: (1) reported FY2026 revenue growth (+84-87%) is a consolidation/mix effect from booking full company-managed store sales rather than organic franchise growth; (2) reported FCF has been negative or near-zero in 4 of the last 5 years and the FY2026 apparent improvement is partly a cash-flow-statement RECLASSIFICATION (principal lease receipts moved from investing to operating, +$4.147m) not repeatable operating improvement; (3) shareholders' equity is negative, ruling out book-value anchors. This model instead: (a) uses system-wide store sales / franchise-ex-Dairygold revenue growth (~22-23% FY2026, decelerating over 10 years to a mature mid-single-digit rate) as the growth driver, NOT reported revenue growth; (b) builds owner FCF bottom-up each year from an EBITDA margin path that first compresses (managed-store mix drag from Dairygold/Tesco ramp) then partially recovers (franchise network scale/overhead leverage as the 300-store FY2034 target is pursued), less D&A, a net IFRS16 lease cash cost (principal+interest paid to landlords net of what CCC recovers via franchisee subleases), bank debt interest, a cash tax rate ramping from the current 0% (large unrecognised tax-loss shield) toward the NZ statutory 28%, CapEx (elevated near-term for managed-store fitouts, fading as growth reverts to capital-light franchising), and a working-capital capture on revenue growth; (c) discounts at a heavily stacked ~18% WACC reflecting nano-cap illiquidity, single-brand/two-market concentration, negative equity/going-concern history, and franchisee-credit/consumer-discretionary cyclicality; (d) uses a 10-year explicit horizon because the owner-FCF margin is still maturing through roughly Year 7 in the base case; (e) caps the Gordon terminal value at a 12x FCF multiple (Gordon does not bind at any scenario tested). The resulting valuation should be read as a genuinely bearish base case for a company trading substantially on growth-story optionality (UAE/India master franchises, Tesco/Dairygold managed-store scaling, 300-store FY2034 target) that a component-built DCF, appropriately risk-adjusted for a nano-cap with negative equity, does not yet capture in current cash generation.

historical_growth.note_units: 1-for-15 share consolidation effective 30 March 2022 -- no per-share metric (EPS) is compared across that break.
historical_growth.revenue_cagr_warning: NOT USED AS GROWTH DRIVER. FY2026 revenue growth is a consolidation/mix effect (company-managed Dairygold/Tesco Ireland store sales now booked gross), not organic growth -- see data_quality_warnings.
historical_growth.store_sales_source: GroupStoreSalesUKIreland kpi (system-wide UK & Ireland store sales, the metric management itself uses to describe underlying growth): FY2022 $53.6m -> FY2023 $49.5m (-7.6%, COVID-recovery base effect) -> FY2024 $58.2m (+17.6%) -> FY2025 $79.6m (+36.8%) -> FY2026 $95.8m (+22.8%).
historical_growth.equity_cagr_note: NOT MEANINGFUL/NOT USED. Shareholders' equity is negative in FY2024, FY2025 and FY2026 (and was only NZ$1.4-3.1m, thin, in FY2022-23); a CAGR through and across a sign change is undefined. This directly overrides the skill's default 'equity CAGR is the primary growth-rate source' rule -- flagged per the task's explicit instruction.
historical_growth.eps_cagr_note: Not computed: FY2022-24 all loss-making (EPS -0.01c, -5.97c, -10.87c), FY2025/26 barely profitable (1.30c, 0.62c) and DOWN 52% YoY. A CAGR across a loss-to-thin-profit transition with a declining tail is not a usable input.
historical_growth.fcf_cagr_note: Underlying FCF (ex the FY2026 lease-receipt reclassification, computed directly from primary cash flow statements): FY2022 -$0.76m, FY2023 -$0.54m, FY2024 +$1.07m, FY2025 -$0.64m, FY2026 +$0.23m. The series crosses zero multiple times; a CAGR is not meaningful. This is itself informative: there is no stable FCF trend to extrapolate, which is why the DCF is built from EBITDA components rather than a historical FCF growth rate.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: franchise_ex_dairygold_growth_fy26 (system-wide store sales / core-franchise growth), decelerating over the 10-year explicit forecast -- see assumptions.base.growth_rates. Equity, EPS and reported-revenue CAGRs are all disclaimed above as unusable for this company.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity, EPS and reported-revenue growth all diverge massively from each other and from store-sales growth (negative equity, volatile EPS, consolidation-inflated revenue) -- this is why none of the standard CAGR anchors is used as the primary driver; store-sales/franchise growth is the only metric with a coherent, explainable trend.

bull.narrative: UAE (min. 50 stores/10yr) and India master franchises begin contributing meaningfully; Regional Developer model successfully extended to Scotland/N.Ireland/West Midlands; Tesco Ireland and Dairygold partnerships expand beyond the initial signed sites; franchise (high-margin) mix reasserts faster, EBITDA margin recovers to ~15% by Year 10 vs ~11.5% FY26 normalised.

bear.narrative: Managed-store margin drag persists (Dairygold/Tesco economics disappoint), UK Regional Developer appointments for Scotland/NI/West Midlands continue to stall, franchisee failures rise (as already seen in the 3 UK store closures/H1 FY26 bad debts), UAE/India master franchises produce negligible near-term contribution, continued dilutive equity raises required to fund working capital.

premiums.nanocap_illiquidity_note: Market cap ~NZ$11.4m -- far below even a NZ$300m small-cap threshold used elsewhere in this project; dual-listed NZX/AQSE with management's own disclosure describing UK trading liquidity as 'still low'.
premiums.concentration_note: Single-brand (Esquires) concentration across essentially two core markets (UK ~52%, Ireland ~42% of segment revenue); International (Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Portugal, Jordan, emerging UAE/India) is <5% of the business today.
premiums.negative_equity_going_concern_note: Shareholders' equity negative since FY2024 (NZ$(1.897)m FY2026); the FY2026 annual report explicitly notes the financial statements 'do not include any adjustments relating to the recoverability...should the Group be unable to continue as a going concern'; history of impairments (Triple Two goodwill NZ$2.385m FY2023, Triple Two disposal loss NZ$3.352m FY2024).
premiums.franchisee_credit_and_cyclicality_note: Revenue depends on franchisee solvency (H1 FY2026 already recorded a $219k loss from 3 UK store closures including $151k bad debts); UK/Irish coffee-shop spend is consumer-discretionary and input-cost/wage-inflation sensitive.

wacc_rationale.wacc_bull_bear_spread: +/-2.0pp applied uniformly to the base stacked WACC for bull/bear scenarios.

bear.intrinsic_value_note: Raw DCF equity value is NEGATIVE (NZ$-0.450m / NZ$-0.0042 per share) in the bear scenario -- the model computes that in a genuine downside case (persistent margin drag, stalled expansion, continued dilution) CCC's enterprise value would not cover even its modest net debt. Floored at NZ$0.00 for display since equity cannot trade negative; the negative raw figure is retained here as the honest underlying signal.

base.note: Entry price (NZ$0.087) sits ABOVE the base-case intrinsic value (NZ$0.070) because the 15% IRR hurdle is BELOW the 18.05% base WACC -- consistent with the skill's sanity property (lower hurdle rate than WACC => entry price above IV, not below).

sensitivity.note: Base-case intrinsic value (NZ$/share) across WACC (rows) and terminal growth (columns).

sanity_check.methodology: Historical trading multiples (P/S, EV/EBITDA; P/E where profitable; P/B disclaimed) computed using the CURRENT market price against each historical year's fundamentals (no historical daily price series available for this nano-cap/dual-listed name, so this is a trailing-multiple-at-current-price proxy, not a true historical multiple time series), compared against the multiple implied by dividing the base-case intrinsic value equity value by FY2026 actual EBITDA/revenue at TODAY's share count.

historical_multiples.p_b_by_year: NOT USABLE - shareholders equity negative FY2024-FY2026 (and thin, NZ$1.4-3.1m, in FY2022-23)

implied_multiples_at_base_iv.note: Uses TODAY's share count (66.377m), not the terminal-year diluted count, so this is a like-for-like comparison against the current-price multiples above.

trip_test.trigger: Implied EV/EBITDA at base IV (4.56x) is below the low end of the ex-outlier historical range (9.44x-17.54x) and below the current trading multiple (9.44x). Base IV (NZ$0.0695) is also below the 52-week trading low (NZ$0.165), i.e. the model implies fair value below where the stock has traded at any point in the past year even on a depressed tape.
trip_test.diagnosis: The gap is driven primarily by the stacked ~18% WACC discounting a still-modest absolute owner-FCF stream (Year-1 owner FCF ~NZ$0.54m vs FY2026 EBITDA NZ$1.39m) over a 10-year horizon, compounded by ~3.5%/yr projected dilution (terminal shares 93.6m vs 66.4m today, a 1.41x increase). The Gordon terminal value does NOT bind against the 12x cap in any scenario (base implied exit multiple 6.6x, bull 7.9x, bear 5.5x -- all well under the cap), so the terminal-value mechanism is not the cause; sensitivity testing confirms IV is highly WACC-sensitive (NZ$0.098 at 15% WACC vs NZ$0.070 at 18.05% WACC) and much less sensitive to the terminal cap choice.
trip_test.fix_applied: Capex and net-lease-cash-cost assumptions were revised DOWN from an initial flat-percent-of-revenue build (which had produced an even lower IV of ~NZ$0.043, implying an EV/EBITDA of just 3.3x) once cross-checked against the filings: the FY2026 elevated capex/lease-cost intensity is tied to the current managed-store (Dairygold/Tesco) ramp, not to the eventual 300-store network which is overwhelmingly franchised/capital-light (new store fitout income to CCC is only NZ$11k -- franchisees fund their own fitouts). Fading capex_pct and lease_net_cash_pct faster as the franchise mix reasserts raised base IV from NZ$0.043 to NZ$0.070 (+60%) and raised the implied EV/EBITDA from 3.3x to 4.6x -- narrowing but not eliminating the gap to the current 9.4x.
trip_test.remaining_gap_disposition: NOT further forced to match the current multiple. The stacked WACC (18.05%) and each of its four components are independently justified by disclosed facts (market cap ~NZ$11.4m, negative equity with an explicit going-concern note in the FY2026 accounts, single-brand/two-market concentration, franchisee credit risk already crystallising in FY2026 bad debts) and are not adjusted merely to close the gap to the market price. The remaining divergence is interpreted as the market pricing meaningful weight on unproven optionality (UAE/India master franchises, Tesco/Dairygold managed-store scaling, the 300-store FY2034 target) that a component-built cash flow DCF, discounted at a rate appropriate to a nano-cap with negative equity, does not yet capture -- consistent with the task's explicit instruction that a negative-upside result is a legitimate outcome for a nano-cap trading on a growth story, not to be reverse-engineered away.

sanity_check.direction_note: NOTE: this trip is in the CONSERVATIVE direction - the model implies a LOWER multiple than history, not a higher one. probability_weighted.weight_rationale: Bear weighted above the standard 25% given the confirmed negative-equity/going-concern history, thin absolute profitability (NZ$315k-813k net income), and the FY2026 OCF reclassification that flatters the headline cash-flow trend; bull weighted below standard given the UAE/India optionality is very early-stage (agreements signed May/Dec 2025, no meaningful trading history) and management itself issued no quantitative FY2027 guidance.
